patient.name: Jordan Price
patient.affectEn: pale and anxious, sitting against the bar wall with his hand pressed over his right chest; blood-soaked shirt; breathing fast
patient.speechEn: short phrases because it is hard to breathe; alert, anxious, cooperative

scene.settingEn: Nightclub on Granville Street, Vancouver, at 0120 hrs. Police are on scene and have secured it; the assailant has fled. The loud music has been stopped, the lights are up and the crowd has been pushed back. The patient sits against the bar wall. Police have recovered a folding knife with a 10 cm blade. One patient; no weapons remain in the area.
hazardsEn: possible weapons - the knife has been recovered by police and no weapons remain in the area (confirmed by police)
blood on the patient - exposure risk

bystanders.who: police officer who escorts you in
bystanders.knowsEn: The scene is secure and the assailant has fled. Stabbing critical history if asked: one stab with a folding knife, 10 cm blade, a single thrust - stabbed, not slashed; it happened about 10 minutes before your arrival. The knife has been recovered. No other wounds seen. Police will clear a path through the crowd for the cot if asked.
Staff called 911 and reported heavy bleeding. Nothing else about the patient. Will hold doors or help clear the way if told exactly what to do.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with NRB and nasal cannula
PCP: IV start kit and tubing

dispatchEn: 0120 hrs. Code 3 to a nightclub on Granville Street, Vancouver, for a 27-year-old male stabbed in the chest. Police are ON SCENE and report the scene is secure - the assailant has fled. Hospital is 8 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: single stab wound to the right chest, patient conscious, heavy bleeding reported by staff. Police confirm the scene is secure - do not stage.
arrivalEn: Police meet you at the door and escort you in: the scene is secure and the assailant has fled. The music has been stopped, the lights are up and the crowd has been pushed back. The patient sits on the floor against the bar wall, his hand over his right chest, blood on his shirt. Police have recovered a folding knife with a 10 cm blade. One patient; no weapons remain in the area.
firstLookEn: Conscious 27-year-old male sitting against the bar wall, pale, breathing fast, hand pressed over his right chest, shirt soaked with blood on the right side.

primary.locEn: Alert (AVPU = A). Oriented; anxious; speaks in short phrases and says it is hard to breathe.
primary.airwayEn: Open and clear; he is speaking in short phrases. No blood or foreign material in the mouth.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 28, shallow and laboured. When the chest is exposed: a 2 cm open wound at the right 4th intercostal space, mid-clavicular line, BUBBLING with each breath (sucking chest wound). If the chest is not exposed, give only the rate and quality and do not describe the wound. Once a gloved hand or a seal covers the wound, the bubbling stops. SpO2 89% on room air if checked now.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 118, present, rapid, regular. Blood on the shirt over the right chest wound; no other external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Front: no other wounds; head, neck, abdomen, pelvis, arms and legs unremarkable. The BACK must be checked for an exit wound (sit him forward and look and sweep with a gloved hand): no exit wound and no other wounds. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: pale, cool, moist. Examiner notes - do not volunteer: the chest wound should be covered immediately (gloved hand, then a commercial chest seal or a three-sided occlusive dressing); report seal-four-sided-no-vent if a plain occlusive dressing is taped down on all four sides with no vent, and chest-wound-packed if gauze is packed into the wound. C-spine is not indicated: isolated penetrating trauma, no blunt mechanism, no neurological complaint.

history.ccEn: I got stabbed. Here. It's hard to breathe.

opqrst.oEn: When he stabbed me. About ten minutes before you got here.
opqrst.pEn: Breathing in makes it worse. Nothing makes it better.
opqrst.rEn: Just here at the wound. It doesn't go anywhere else.

sample.sEn: It's hard to breathe. It hurts right here when I breathe in. My heart is racing.
sample.lEn: Wings around eleven. Two beers over the evening.
sample.eEn: A guy stabbed me once with a folding knife and ran. I didn't pass out. I only felt the one stab.

fe.cnsEn: No, nothing like that. No headache, no numbness.
fe.respiratoryEn: I've been short of breath since he stabbed me. It hurts when I breathe in.
fe.cardiovascularEn: No pressure in my chest. My heart is racing.
fe.eentEn: No, nothing. Eyes, ears, nose, throat are fine.

findings.headNeckEn: No injuries. Trachea midline. No JVD at present.
findings.chestLungsEn: Wound at the right 4th intercostal space, mid-clavicular (sealed if the candidate has sealed it; otherwise still bubbling with each breath). On auscultation of all 6 sites: air entry DIMINISHED on the right side; left side clear.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft and non-tender in all four quadrants.
findings.backEn: No exit wound and no other wounds on the back. Any dressings in place are intact.

vitalsSets.spo2: 93% on 15 L NRB (89% on room air before oxygen)

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: en route, seal on (after loading, or 12 minutes into the call)

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: The patient says it is getting harder to breathe, and he looks more anxious.
The patient is becoming much more short of breath and more anxious.
stateChanges.findingsIfAssessedEn: Breath sounds are now ABSENT on the right on auscultation; the SpO2 is falling (the engine gives the reading). If the candidate then lifts or burps the seal, report tension-relieved; if they move on to other tasks without doing so, report tension-not-relieved.

vitalsPatch.spo2: falling on 15 L NRB - lower than the previous reading

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: As the seal is lifted there is a rush of air from the wound, and his breathing eases.
stateChanges.findingsIfAssessedEn: Breath sounds on the right have returned but are still diminished.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan chest seals, trauma dressings, oxygen, early transport
triggers: plan for a sucking chest wound
this will be a load and go

expected.actionEn: Confirm scene security with police before entering; plan PPE
Verbalize hazards (crowd, possible weapons - confirmed clear by police), environment, MOI (10 cm blade stab), one patient
First look: conscious male, sitting, pale, breathing fast, blood-soaked right shirt
Verbalize ruling OUT c-spine: isolated penetrating trauma without blunt MOI or neuro deficit
triggers: did you fall or hit your head
talking so the airway is open

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing AND expose the chest; find the open chest wound
Seal the sucking chest wound IMMEDIATELY (gloved hand, then commercial seal or 3-sided occlusive)

triggers: rate and quality of the pulse

expected.actionEn: Complete the RBS including the BACK - check for an exit wound
Position semi-sitting / position of comfort (no spinal concern) as soon as possible
Categorize as RTC (penetrating torso trauma) and act with urgency
Ready to load within 15 minutes, seal secured before movement
Delegate partner for cot and egress through the crowd; police to clear the path
triggers: police can you clear the crowd

expected.actionEn: Confirm chief complaint: stab wound with difficulty breathing
HxC/C with OPQRRRST plus stabbing critical history (weapon, blade length, number of wounds, time)
triggers: how many times were you stabbed

expected.actionEn: SpO2 with calibration and trend after oxygen
Head/neck exam including trachea and JVD
Chest exam: 6-site auscultation, recognize diminished right air entry
Back exam (exit wound already ruled out - reconfirm dressings)
Wound management skill: correct three-sided/vented chest seal technique
Verbalize tension pneumothorax watch and the burp-the-seal response
triggers: if tension develops I will burp the seal
no Entonox because of the pneumothorax

expected.actionEn: PCP: vascular access en route; TXA criteria verbalized and monitored
triggers: TXA only if he becomes hypotensive

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs, seal integrity and right-side air entry after each move
Respond correctly to any tension pneumothorax development (burp/lift the seal, reassess)
Complete hand-off including seal type and breath-sound trend

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate covers the chest wound - gloved hand over it, a commercial chest seal or a three-sided occlusive dressing (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)

candidate has exposed the chest and seen the bubbling wound, then moves on (to circulation, vitals, history, oxygen or packaging) without first covering it with a gloved hand or a seal (a partner's gloved hand on the wound counts as covered)
candidate tapes a plain occlusive dressing down on all four sides with no vent, instead of a three-sided occlusive dressing or a commercial chest seal
candidate packs gauze into the chest wound

candidate states they are monitoring for tension pneumothorax, checks the trachea or neck veins, rechecks the seal, or states they would burp/lift the seal if tension develops (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)
AFTER the examiner has reported worsening breathing / absent right breath sounds (tension-develops), the candidate lifts, burps or vents the seal to release the trapped air

AFTER the examiner has reported worsening breathing / absent right breath sounds (tension-develops), the candidate's next actions do not lift, burp or vent the seal (e.g. they only increase oxygen, carry on with history or vitals, or say they will wait for the hospital). Do not report it in the same turn the signs are first given.

candidate performs or attempts a needle decompression of the chest, or tells the partner to do one (not in the BC EMR/PCP exam protocols). Requesting ALS or telling the hospital about it is NOT this event.
candidate takes manual c-spine control, applies a hard collar, or places the patient on a spinal device (not indicated: isolated penetrating trauma, no blunt mechanism, no neurological complaint)
candidate lets or asks the patient to stand up or walk (e.g. to the cot or out to the ambulance)
PCP runs a saline bolus past 500 mL, or onto the next 500 mL, without reassessing the patient (BP / vitals / ABCs) in between
candidate checks the back / posterior chest for an exit wound

drugs.doseEn: self-administered by inhalation - CONTRAINDICATED in this scenario: pneumothorax (open chest wound). A statement of withholding it is NOT drug:entonox.
2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute - NOT indicated at present: give only if shock from blood loss develops (SBP under 90); verbalize the criteria and monitor
drugs.indicationsEn: major trauma after initiating the Hypovolemia protocol; signs of shock with mechanism or findings suggesting ongoing bleeding - currently BP 104/70, criteria not met
drugs.contraindicationsEn: known hypersensitivity or allergy to TXA; more than 3 hours after injury; patient under 12 years; isolated TBI
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

drugs.doseEn: vascular access en route; a fluid bolus (20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL) only if hypotension or hypoperfusion develops
500 - 1000 mg PO for mild to moderate pain; not part of the expected care in this RTC penetrating chest trauma
300 - 400 mg PO for mild to moderate pain; not part of the expected care in this RTC penetrating chest trauma

deduct.errorEn: Conducts a RBS but it is out of sequence and it may affect negatively on patient care (e.g. – delay of performing the RBS whereby they found injuries late, dressings are not secured or if direct pressure is not maintained with bandages immediately after the primary survey.)
Chooses the wrong dressing for the wound (e.g. does not use a burn dressing for burns)
Does not meet the standards for wound management detrimental to patient care (e.g. does not apply a chest seal to sucking chest wound)
Does not perform an act that was required based on patient presentation that is detrimental to patient care
Performs an act that may jeopardize the life/limb of the patient that is not already captured in the major performance criteria (e.g. performing chest compressions on a patient with a pulse)
C-spine control taken when not indicated by mechanism of Injury

Performs an act that could aggravate the patient's condition or injury that is not already captured in the major performance criteria (e.g. excessively bumping a fractured leg which causes gross movement and pain)
Does not rule out all the contraindications, detrimental to patient care
Performs the protocol with isolated error with potential to be detrimental to patient care
Performs the protocol with isolated error with potential to be detrimental to patient care
Initiated protocol without proper indications (e.g. patient is not DLOC)
Initiated protocol without proper indications (e.g. patient is not DLOC)
Deduction if the candidate does not check for an exit wound in a patient with an open chest wound.

handoffFacts.finalVitals: GCS 15, BP 100/68, pulse 116, resps 26 shallow, skin pale cool moist, SpO2 94% on 15 L NRB; air entry diminished on the right but stable, trachea midline, no JVD

examinerPrompts.breathingNotDepictedEn: The actor cannot show the wound bubbling or the work of breathing: if the candidate exposes the chest, state that there is a 2 cm open wound at the right 4th intercostal space, mid-clavicular, bubbling with each breath, and that respirations are shallow and laboured.
examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: You exposed the chest earlier - what did you see on the right side of the chest, and what did you find on his back?

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: identical priorities - seal in the primary, exit-wound check, high-flow O2, tension watch, 15-minute packaging. No IV, no TXA. Entonox remains contraindicated at every level. Needle decompression is not in the BC EMR exam protocols - a developing tension pneumothorax is managed by burping or lifting the seal.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds en-route vascular access and TXA 2 g IV only if hemorrhagic shock criteria are met; Functional Enquiry en route. If ventilation becomes necessary, be ready to disconnect and manage a developing tension pneumothorax first. Needle decompression is not in the BC PCP exam protocols - a developing tension pneumothorax is managed by burping or lifting the seal. Entonox is contraindicated (pneumothorax).

sourcePages: scenario tr-03 (data/practical/scenarios.json); BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 RTC criteria (major penetrating trauma to the head, neck, torso; cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock), p.19 Wound Care (expose and examine; do not pack wounds on the neck, chest, or abdomen), p.25 Spinal Management (NEXUS / Canadian C-Spine indications), p.34 Chest Trauma (control bleeding with gauze; seal an open chest wound with a three-sided occlusive dressing or commercial chest seal and monitor closely for tension pneumothorax, relieve if necessary; PCP en route: vascular access if required, TXA if indicated), p.54 Hypovolemia (SBP < 90; PCP: fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 litres reassessing every 500 mL; consider TXA in shock secondary to blood loss), p.58 Acetaminophen and p.68 Ibuprofen (mild to moderate pain), p.65 Entonox (contraindication: pneumothorax), p.78 Tranexamic Acid (2 g / 2000 mg IV push over 1 minute; contraindicated > 3 hours after injury, < 12 years, isolated TBI)
